clue.text: Puff away, not fit any more?

definitions.meaning: to puff away is to breathe out, to blow air from the lungs
read cryptically as EX- (former) plus HALE (fit, healthy): once healthy, no longer so

explanation.surface: Someone wheezing on a cigarette wonders whether they have lost their fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split the word as ex-hale, 'formerly hale', and hale means fit and healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out is puffing air away from the lungs, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Caught in impasse, organised retreat into fantasy

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter within the rearranged word
organised says the letters of impasse are put into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a deadlock plans an orderly withdrawal into dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into ESAPISM, a rearrangement of IMPASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is the habit of fleeing reality into daydreams and fantasy.

clue.text: Woman's accessory lands on back of ankle that gets grazed

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces land on top of what follows

parts.note: her is the possessive used for a woman
a bag is a typical fashion accessory

indicators.note: back of picks out the final letter of ankle

explanation.surface: A handbag drops onto someone's ankle and scrapes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and green plants, the vegetation that livestock graze.

clue.text: Desperate to survive, died before long

indicators.note: before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: to last is to survive, to endure
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Someone frantic to stay alive died after a lingering wish.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a desperate final attempt when all else has failed.

clue.text: A crossbar's small diameter replaced arbitrarily

indicators.note: replaced says the letter for small is swapped out and the letter for diameter goes in its place

parts.note: a transom is a horizontal crossbar, as over a door or window
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
D is the standard abbreviation for diameter in geometry

explanation.surface: An engineer notes that a beam was fitted with a part of the wrong width.
explanation.walkthrough: A transom is the bar over a door or window; 'replaced' swaps the small letter for the diameter letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something arbitrarily means choosing without plan or reason, haphazardly.

clue.text: Endpiece belonging to part of shoe not quite remembered here

parts.note: a tip is the end piece of something
of shows belonging, as in the end of the road
the tongue is the flap of a shoe under the laces

explanation.surface: A cobbler describes the end of a shoe's flap.
explanation.walkthrough: A word on the tip of your tongue is one you almost, but not quite, recall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something nearly recalled but just out of reach of memory.

clue.text: Correspond with a nameless party member

indicators.note: nameless says the abbreviation for name, a single letter, is dropped

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party

explanation.surface: Exchanging letters with an anonymous political activist.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name; GREEN without it is GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to tally or match, as two accounts correspond.

clue.text: Put down, say, and land for one's own benefit

indicators.note: say signals that the word for belittle is pronounced to give the answer

parts.note: to demean is to belittle or put down

explanation.surface: Someone belittles others and grabs land for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne was the manorial land kept by the lord for his own use.

clue.text: Money is low (a pound), cash regularly being wasted

parts.note: to low is the cow's call, to moo
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: every other letter of cash is thrown away, keeping the rest at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A rueful note that funds are short because money keeps being squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of cash leaves AH.
explanation.definitionFit: Moolah is slang for money, cash or dosh.

clue.text: His shots had entire crossbar twanging

indicators.note: a twanging bar vibrates and jumps about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer's shots kept hitting the woodwork with a twang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shots' looks like football but means photographs. Henri Cartier-Bresson was the great French photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition names the man by his work: a photographer known for his shots.

clue.text: Trickster has a way quietly to stop complaint

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so these pieces fill a gap inside the grumble

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault, here taken as the grumble itself
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
SH is the call for quiet, hush

explanation.surface: A con artist hushes up a grumble before it can spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To stop' means to plug, as a cork stops a bottle; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sharp cheats at cards, a classic kind of trickster or swindler.

clue.text: Lover of the church needing nothing more

parts.note: Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church, as in 'converting to Rome'
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A devout believer needs nothing beyond their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing ... more' simply adds O on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo gave his name to any ardent male lover or womaniser.

clue.text: Cheer as Archbishop enters Hell?

indicators.note: enters says one name goes inside the other word

parts.note: the pit is an old name for hell, the bottomless pit
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether a churchman going to hell deserves applause.
explanation.walkthrough: Laud was executed in 1645, which lends the surface its dark joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or applause, a cheer of approval.

clue.text: Plant failing initially easier to replace

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of failing
to re-place letters is to put them in new places, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A gardener decides a dying shrub would be simpler to swap out.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a fragrant flowering plant grown from corms.

clue.text: Made up a word for cereal

definitions.meaning: formed a word letter by letter, the British past tense of spell
a primitive species of wheat grown as a grain crop

explanation.surface: Someone invented a new term to name a breakfast grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: past tense of spell, and an ancient wheat.

clue.text: Communication system Number Ten backed

parts.note: read as num-ber, something that numbs: ether was an early anaesthetic

indicators.note: backed means the word ten is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A phone network at Downing Street, the Prime Minister's Number Ten, has been funded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a numeral but 'one that numbs', and Number Ten splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard networking technology linking computers in local networks.

clue.text: Extra fee is concerning one just up

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a fresher is a first-year student, just come up to university

explanation.surface: An extra charge relates to a newly arrived student.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, students 'go up' to university; a refresher is an extra fee paid to a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is an additional fee paid to counsel during a long case.

clue.text: Smelling most strongly of drink, most advisable to swallow vast amount of water

indicators.note: to swallow means to take something inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: best means most advisable, as in 'you had best go'
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A drinker reeking of booze is advised to gulp down plenty of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Beery means smelling of beer; the superlative is the most strongly so.

clue.text: Characters that can be incomprehensibly in the soup

definitions.text: Characters that can be incomprehensibly in the soup

parts.words: Characters that can be incomprehensibly in the soup
parts.note: letters are characters; pasta letters float in a children's soup, and a jumble of acronyms is called by the same soup name

explanation.surface: Letters floating, jumbled and unreadable, in a bowl of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' usually means in trouble; here it points to alphabet soup, pasta letters, and to the jargon of initials nobody understands.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of letters used in writing, so a set of written characters.

clue.text: One said to be without coat for protection

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken that matches the answer's sound

parts.note: with One, someone who lacks, to lack being to be without

explanation.surface: Someone is reportedly left without a coat to protect them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ... to be without' is a lacker, one who lacks; spoken, it matches the varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a hard glossy varnish applied as a protective coating.

clue.text: Fine sort of seaman's yarn

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
an able seaman is a rank of sailor in the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor spins a good tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a story, often invented, much as a yarn is a tall tale.

clue.text: City living enthrals one — and the next character

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: being means existing or living
I is the Roman numeral one
J is the letter following I in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Urban life captivates a person and the stranger after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Beijing is the capital city of China.

clue.text: Shop doesn't have this underwear, but stall does

definitions.text: Shop doesn't have this underwear, but stall does

parts.words: Shop doesn't have this underwear, but stall does
parts.note: the word stall contains two lower-case letter l's, little ells, while shop has none

explanation.surface: A market stall sells undies that the shop does not stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as small Ls: stall holds two small (lower-case) l's, shop none. Smalls is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls is a British informal word for underclothes.

clue.text: In absence of cat, players about to steal something much smaller

indicators.note: In at the head of the clue places the following pieces within the playful rodents

parts.note: from the proverb 'when the cat's away the mice will play': mice are the players
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: While the cat is away, mischievous creatures plot a small theft.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'when the cat's away, the mice will play' supplies the players; 'about' is circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe is a microscopic organism, far tinier than any mouse.

clue.text: Bore a daughter, cradling classically beautiful girl

indicators.note: cradling means holding within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A mother gave birth to a girl and now cradles her lovely child.
explanation.definitionFit: An oread is a mountain nymph of Greek myth, a beautiful girl of classical legend.

clue.text: Wanting more to be killed, should never admit it?

indicators.note: admit means let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never
to die is to be killed, lose one's life

explanation.surface: A grim question about someone longing to be killed who would never confess it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Should' and 'it' are only links; 'admit' means let in.
explanation.definitionFit: Needier is the comparative of needy, so lacking or wanting more.

clue.text: See advantage in parasite

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see! or behold!
use means benefit or advantage, as in 'of no use'

explanation.surface: Someone finds a benefit in a freeloader.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless insect living as a parasite on its host.

clue.text: Messy feature of thaw unlikely to appear in print

definitions.text: Messy feature of thaw unlikely to appear in print

parts.words: Messy feature of thaw unlikely to appear in print
parts.note: melting snow leaves heaps of mush; a publisher's heap of unsolicited manuscripts is unlikely to be printed

explanation.surface: Melting snow piles up in mucky heaps that nobody will publish.
explanation.walkthrough: A slush pile is the stack of unsolicited submissions that publishers rarely accept; the thaw picture is a literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishers call their heap of unrequested manuscripts by this name; few ever get printed.

clue.text: To open up implant is clear and urgent

indicators.note: to open up something is to split it, with another piece sitting in the gap

parts.note: a stent is a tube implanted to keep a vessel open
to rid is to clear, as in rid the house of mice

explanation.surface: A surgeon insists that a heart device must be unblocked without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: A stent is a mesh tube put into an artery; 'is' and 'and' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and insistent, pressing its demand urgently.

clue.text: Intelligent economist

definitions.meaning: John ..., the Victorian radical who campaigned for free trade and against the Corn Laws

explanation.surface: Praise for a clever economist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means clever, and John Bright was a famous free-trade campaigner.
